newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura ex-president arrested over racketeer affair.
newsitem.headline: Nomura ex-president arrested over racketeer affair.

text.p: Tokyo prosecutors on Friday arrested former Nomura Securities Co Ltd president Hideo Sakamaki in connection with a scandal involving allegedly illegal payoffs to a racketeer.

Sakamaki, who stepped down as president in March and is now an adviser to the leading brokerage, told a parliamentary panel this week that he had briefly met the alleged corporate racketeer at the heart of the scandal, Ryuichi Koike, in 1992, but denied knowledge of any stock deals by Koike through Nomura.

The scandal -- the second involving Nomura in six years -- has dealt a blow not only to the brokerage's bottom line but also to the already tarnished image of Japan's financial institutions at a critical time as they prepare to compete in Tokyo's increasingly deregulated markets.

Earlier this month Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), filed a complaint with prosecutors against Nomura, two former Nomura executives and a company official alleging they had illegally compensated a firm run by Koike's younger brother Yoshinori.
Prosecutors arrested the two former Nomura executives and the company official as well as the two Koike brothers.

Prosecutors are also investigating one of Japan's biggest banks, Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB), in connection with the Nomura scandal. Top DKB executives have stepped down to take responsibility for the bank's improper loans to the younger Koike and his company.
